sectionTitle: Six years, one throughline: make the system do the repetitive part.

roles.role: IT Service Desk & Technical Operations Specialist
roles.highlight: Ran Tier 1 and Tier 2 support for internal users across Windows, macOS, Microsoft 365 and production publishing systems.
contributions: Owned service desk tickets end to end — intake, troubleshooting, escalation, testing, user communication, resolution.
Triaged by real business impact: urgency, production deadlines and number of users affected, not queue order.
Diagnosed application access, permissions, publishing failures, broken links, VPN and production issues using logs, dev tools and system state.
Escalated to engineering with reproduction steps, screenshots, impact and the troubleshooting already done — so the receiving team started from something useful.
Wrote the Confluence knowledge base: troubleshooting guides, release instructions and SOPs.
Spotted recurring ticket patterns and took them to engineering as fixes rather than re-answering them.

roles.highlight: Built and launched 175+ academic and magazine sites, and wrote the Python that cut manual image editing by 40%.
contributions: Built and launched 175+ academic and magazine sites in Cascade CMS — templating, content workflows, responsive deployment.
Developed custom WordPress themes and plugins with SEO, caching and analytics dashboards.
Designed Figma wireframes and prototypes, then built them out in responsive HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
Automated image workflows in Python and OpenCV — HDR pipelines, content-aware crop, dynamic resizing — cutting manual editing time by 40%.
Applied computer vision across 2,500+ archived magazine pages to score relevance, retiring 1,600+ obsolete assets with a full audit trail.
Lifted content engagement roughly 15% using A/B testing, Qualtrics surveys and GA4.
Ran responsive, functional, accessibility, browser and production QA before and after every release.
Supported faculty and campus partners on Microsoft 365, Cascade CMS and endpoint issues alongside the development work.

roles.highlight: Two years of campus photography, published in the University of Dayton Magazine and on official university channels.
contributions: Shot campus and event photography across every season and every kind of weather.
Official event photographer for the NCAA Men's Basketball Championship First Four in March 2025, shooting courtside.
Produced marketing visuals, infographics and animated banners in Photoshop, Illustrator and After Effects.
Integrated multimedia into Cascade CMS and WordPress alongside the sites I was building.

roles.highlight: Managed 40+ academic and campaign microsites in WordPress, and was named Employee of the Month.
contributions: Managed 40+ academic and campaign microsites in WordPress (PHP/MySQL), with HubSpot wired in for lead capture and tracking.
Designed UX wireframes in Figma and converted them into CMS-ready templates for responsive publishing.
Customised themes and optimised for SEO and accessibility, with Google Analytics for performance monitoring.
Built GPU-accelerated diagnostic scripts in CUDA and OpenCL to automate detection of login, network and system issues, cutting ticket turnaround.
Kept IT services running through high-priority events such as placement drives.

roles.highlight: Built patient-facing booking portals and provider search flows to WCAG/ADA standards.
contributions: Designed and developed responsive booking portals, provider search flows and service-line microsites, mobile-first.
Built front-end components — forms, navigation, interactive cards — with real validation, states and error handling.
Implemented schema.org markup and WCAG/ADA compliance with the marketing and SEO teams.
Ran UX research using GA4, heatmaps and usability testing, iterating layouts and CTAs on the appointment funnel.
Optimised page performance, load times and cross-browser compatibility.

roles.highlight: Corporate site, investor pages and project showcase microsites, built responsive from scratch.
contributions: Designed and launched corporate layouts, investor pages and project showcase microsites.
Built responsive front-end interfaces in HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript for cross-browser and multi-device support.
Built interactive UI components — sliders, forms, navigation, project galleries.
Integrated SEO best practice, analytics tracking and structured data markup.
Established scalable templates for later digital work.
